label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, secret-rotation, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 8 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy webhook-receiver: WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION v2 -> v1); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: secret-rotation
case.title: The books stop catching up: our webhook receiver refuses every webhook
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the webhook receiver with a rotated secret the provider does not sign with (WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, while the provider signs with v1): every webhook fails its signature check and is refused with a 400, so no event reaches Kafka, and the provider keeps sending them again, with backoff.
case.remedy: roll the webhook receiver back to v1 (or accept both versions until the provider signs with v2): the provider sends every refused webhook again, and the books catch up by themselves

expected_symptoms: the books cannot catch up with the provider: the money check cannot settle, the provider's webhooks not acknowledged, and the books rule fires at its second evaluation, about 50 s after the deploy
the receiver refuses every webhook with a 400, counts it as bad_signature and logs 'webhook refused: bad signature'; the provider sends its growing backlog again and again, tens of times a second
nothing new is booked or confirmed, and both consumers' lag stays at 0: nothing reaches Kafka

payments and refunds still go through, but one whose answer was lost cannot be confirmed: its client's retries get 503 again, so the 5xx share of POST /payments about doubles and its p95 climbs to about 0.6 s, both under their thresholds

after the rollback the books catch up within about three minutes: the provider sends each refused webhook again within a minute of its last try, and one whose acknowledgement is then lost (the traffic's noise) a minute later
fault.remedy: roll the webhook receiver back to v1 (or accept both versions until the provider signs with v2): the provider sends every refused webhook again, and the books catch up by themselves

alert.name: BooksBehindProvider
alert.summary: Our books cannot catch up with the provider: at each of the last 2 evaluations, the money check waited 15 s and could not settle up to its cutoff. At the last one, 187 of the provider's webhooks up to it had not been acknowledged yet.

diagnosis.hypothesis: The webhook-receiver was redeployed at 07:24:43 with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. Since then it rejects almost every webhook from the provider as bad_signature, apparently because the provider still signs with the old secret. Rejected webhooks are never acknowledged, so the provider keeps resending them and the rejections keep climbing. Nothing reaches Kafka, so ledger-consumer and payment-confirmer get no events. The books fall behind the provider and the money check cannot settle to its cutoff, which is why BooksBehindProvider fired. The consumers look healthy, so the fault is at the receiver's signature check.

evidence.shows: The only service changed after the initial 07:23:16 startup is webhook-receiver, redeployed at 07:24:43 with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. The other services' settings are unchanged.
bad_signature climbs from 139 to 1629 between 07:24:57 and 07:25:57, while the queued count is stuck at 246 from 07:24:37 on. Accepted webhooks stopped right after the redeploy.
All containers are running and healthy with no restarts, so a crash or outage does not explain the backlog.
No ERROR logs from webhook-receiver in the last 10 minutes. The rejections are counted in metrics but not logged as errors, so they are easy to miss.

The money check with wait=false failed. 281 provider events from evt_000264 onward were posted 0 times (lost), and the ledger is $12,910.38 below the provider. 7 payments are pending in our records but charged by the provider. The ledger is still balanced and refunds match the provider. This is the pattern of events that never arrived, not of mis-booked ones.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll webhook-receiver back to the settings it ran before the 07:24:43 deploy, with the previous secret version, so signatures from the provider verify again. The provider resends unacknowledged webhooks, so the backlog should then be accepted, queued and booked by both consumers. After the rollback, check that bad_signature stops growing and queued resumes, then run money_check with wait=true to confirm all five invariants pass. If the provider was instead meant to move to v2, the secret change should be coordinated with it rather than left on one side only.

diagnosis.blast_radius: The receiver restarts and pauses briefly, during which the provider's retries just wait. Only webhook intake is affected. The rollback repairs nothing already booked, but nothing was booked wrongly here, since the events were never queued. The backlog should replay through the provider's retries. Not confirmed: which secret the provider actually signs with. No log or tool output shows it, and this is inferred from the timing of the failures.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rollback does not stop the bad_signature rejections, or makes things worse, redeploy webhook-receiver with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2 and check with the provider which secret version it is signing with. Then align the two sides.
